title: Unit 4 test: Contextual Applications of Differentiation
author: bc-tests-foundation
directions: This original practice test reports raw points only. Work without a calculator in Section I Part A and Section II Part B. A graphing calculator is allowed in the other parts. Angles are in radians. Give exact answers without a calculator and numerical answers to three decimal places when needed. Show mathematical reasoning on every free-response part.

figures.alt: Velocity graph with time in seconds and velocity in meters per second. Straight segments connect (0, −3), (1, −4), (3, 2), and (4, 1).

parts.title: No calculator
parts.directions: Choose one answer for each question. No calculator is allowed.

items.prompt: The concentration C(t), in milligrams per liter, depends on time t in hours. What does C′(6) = −0.4 mean?
choices: At 6 hours, concentration is decreasing at 0.4 milligrams per liter per hour.
At 6 hours, the concentration equals −0.4 milligrams per liter.
At 6 hours, time decreases by 0.4 hours per milligram per liter.
Over the first 6 hours, concentration decreased by 0.4 milligrams per liter.
items.rationale: The negative sign describes decreasing concentration at that instant; the derivative units are (mg/L)/hour.

distractorNotes.B: Confuses the derivative with the concentration itself.
distractorNotes.C: Reverses the dependent and independent quantities and their units.
distractorNotes.D: An instantaneous rate at 6 does not determine the total change since time zero.

items.prompt: A particle has position s(t) = t^3 − 9t^2 + 24t meters, where t is in seconds. At t = 5, which statement is true?
choices: It moves in the negative direction and speeds up.
It moves in the positive direction and slows down.
It moves in the positive direction and speeds up.
It moves in the negative direction and slows down.
items.rationale: v(5) = 3(25) − 18(5) + 24 = 9 m/s and a(5) = 30 − 18 = 12 m/s². Positive velocity gives direction, and matching signs give increasing speed.

distractorNotes.A: The velocity at 5 is positive, not negative.
distractorNotes.B: Velocity and acceleration have the same positive sign, so speed increases.
distractorNotes.D: Both its direction and its speed trend are misread.

items.prompt: The sides x and y of a rectangle change with time. At one instant x = 3 cm, y = 5 cm, dx/dt = 2 cm/s, and dy/dt = −1 cm/s. What is the rate of change of its area?
choices: 13 cm²/s
7 cm²/s
−2 cm²/s
10 cm²/s
items.rationale: A = xy gives A′ = x′y + xy′ = 2(5) + 3(−1) = 7 cm²/s.

distractorNotes.A: Treats the shrinking side as growing at 1 cm/s.
distractorNotes.C: Multiplies the two rates instead of differentiating xy.
distractorNotes.D: Includes only y dx/dt and ignores the changing second side.

items.prompt: A conical pile always has radius r = h/2. Its volume is V = (π/3)r^2h. Which equation correctly relates its rates after eliminating r?
choices: dV/dt = (π/3)h^2 dh/dt
dV/dt = (π/4)h^3 dh/dt
dV/dt = (π/12)h^2 dh/dt
dV/dt = (π/4)h^2 dh/dt
items.rationale: Substitute r = h/2 to get V = πh^3/12, then differentiate with respect to time.

distractorNotes.A: Retains the original volume coefficient π/3 without accounting for the radius substitution and differentiation.
distractorNotes.B: Does not reduce the power of h after differentiation.
distractorNotes.C: Fails to multiply by 3 when differentiating h^3.

items.prompt: Using the tangent-line approximation to f(x) = x^(1/3) at x = 64, which value estimates 65^(1/3)?

distractorNotes.A: Uses 3(4) instead of 3(4^2) in the derivative denominator.
distractorNotes.B: Treats the derivative of x^(1/3) as the constant 1/3.
distractorNotes.C: Uses a negative input change even though 65 exceeds 64.

items.prompt: What is lim as x→0 of [ln(1 + 3x) − 3x]/x^2?
items.rationale: The original ratio is 0/0. After one application of L’Hôpital’s Rule it remains 0/0. A second gives [−9/(1 + 3x)^2]/2 → −9/2.

distractorNotes.A: Misses the inner derivative 3 in the second differentiation.
distractorNotes.B: Stops after identifying that the first derivatives also give 0/0.
distractorNotes.D: Loses the negative sign when differentiating 3/(1 + 3x).

items.prompt: A student applies L’Hôpital’s Rule to lim as x→1 of (x^2 + 1)/(x + 1) and reports 2. Which response is correct?
choices: The limit is 0; both numerator and denominator are finite.
The limit is 1; the original quotient is not indeterminate.
The limit does not exist; numerator and denominator are both nonzero.
The limit is 2; differentiating numerator and denominator always preserves a limit.
items.rationale: Direct substitution gives 2/2 = 1. The 0/0 or infinite-over-infinite conditions for the rule do not hold.

distractorNotes.A: Finite nonzero numerator and denominator give their ratio, not zero.
distractorNotes.C: A rational function is continuous where its denominator is nonzero.
distractorNotes.D: L’Hôpital’s Rule has indeterminate-form hypotheses that are not satisfied here.

items.prompt: The graph shows a particle’s velocity. At t = 2 seconds, which statement is true?
choices: The particle moves negatively and its speed is decreasing.
The particle moves positively and its speed is decreasing.
The particle moves negatively and its speed is increasing.
The particle moves positively and its speed is increasing.
items.rationale: The segment from (1, −4) to (3, 2) gives v(2) = −1 m/s and a(2) = 3 m/s². Opposite signs mean the speed decreases.

distractorNotes.B: At t = 2 the velocity is below zero, although the graph is rising.
distractorNotes.C: Negative velocity with positive acceleration gives decreasing speed.
distractorNotes.D: Confuses the positive graph slope with positive velocity.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Choose one answer for each question. A graphing calculator is needed for some numerical work.

items.prompt: A spherical bubble has radius 2.7 cm increasing at 0.13 cm/s. Using V = (4π/3)r^3, find dV/dt to three decimal places.
choices: 4.411 cm³/s
3.970 cm³/s
items.rationale: Differentiate with time: dV/dt = 4πr^2 dr/dt = 4π(2.7)^2(0.13) ≈ 11.909 cm³/s.

distractorNotes.A: Uses one power of r instead of r^2 in the surface factor.
distractorNotes.B: Omits the factor 3 when differentiating the cubic volume expression.

items.prompt: Use the tangent line to y = ln x at x = 2 to estimate ln(2.06). What is the estimate to three decimal places?
items.rationale: The linearization is ln 2 + (1/2)(x − 2); at 2.06 it gives ln 2 + 0.03 ≈ 0.723.

distractorNotes.A: Subtracts the linear change instead of adding it.
distractorNotes.C: Uses a slope of 1/4 rather than 1/2.
distractorNotes.D: Adds the full input change rather than multiplying by the slope 1/2.

items.prompt: A particle’s position is s(t) = e^(−t) sin(2t) meters for t ≥ 0 seconds. At what first positive time is it at rest?
items.rationale: v(t) = e^(−t)[2 cos(2t) − sin(2t)]. The first positive root has tan(2t) = 2, so t = arctan(2)/2 ≈ 0.554 s.

distractorNotes.B: Solves cos(2t) = 0 while omitting the exponential product-rule term.
distractorNotes.D: Solves for 2t but does not divide the result by 2.

items.prompt: Which value equals lim as x→∞ of ln(1 + 4x)/ln(1 + 7x)?
items.rationale: The ratio has infinite-over-infinite form. L’Hôpital’s Rule gives [4/(1 + 4x)]/[7/(1 + 7x)], whose limit is 1.

distractorNotes.A: Assumes the larger coefficient forces the denominator to have a higher growth order.
distractorNotes.B: Uses the ratio 4/7 of the coefficients without accounting for logarithmic growth.
distractorNotes.C: Reverses the coefficient ratio and still ignores logarithmic growth.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Show the equations used for numerical results and include units where appropriate.

items.prompt: A camera is fixed at ground level 35 meters horizontally from a vertical mast. A marker on the mast has height h(t) = 2t^2 + 3t meters for t ≥ 0 seconds. The elevation angle θ satisfies tan θ = h/35, with 0 ≤ θ < π/2.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find dθ/dt at t = 4, in radians per second. Show the equation relating the rates.

rubric.criterion: Differentiates the angle-height relation with both time derivatives.

steps: Differentiate tan θ = h/35: sec^2 θ · θ′ = h′/35.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the tangent line to θ(t) at t = 4 to estimate θ(4.05).

rubric.criterion: Finds θ(4) using the angle relation.
Uses the tangent estimate with increment 0.05.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Let d be the straight-line distance from camera to marker. Find dd/dt at t = 4 and explain the sign.

rubric.criterion: Builds and differentiates the right-triangle distance model.
Explains the positive sign as increasing distance.

parts.answer: 14.869 m/s, positive because the camera-marker distance is increasing.
steps: Both h and h′ are positive at this time.

parts.title: No calculator
parts.directions: Show your reasoning and give exact answers. No calculator is allowed.

items.prompt: Define F(t) = (e^(2t) − 1)/t for t ≠ 0, and choose F(0) so that F is continuous at 0.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find F(0), showing that the hypotheses for L’Hôpital’s Rule hold for the limit you use.

rubric.criterion: Identifies 0/0 and the differentiability/nonzero denominator-derivative conditions.
Obtains 2 and assigns it to F(0).

steps: As t→0, the numerator and denominator both approach zero; they are differentiable near zero and the denominator derivative is 1.
Its limit is 2, so continuity requires F(0) = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the definition of the derivative to find F′(0). Justify any repeated use of L’Hôpital’s Rule.

rubric.criterion: Forms the correct derivative quotient using F(0) = 2.
Checks the indeterminate forms and applies the rule twice correctly.

steps: It is 0/0, and after differentiating once gives (2e^(2h) − 2)/(2h), still 0/0.
A second application gives 4e^(2h)/2 → 2; all functions are differentiable in a punctured neighborhood and the relevant denominator derivatives are nonzero there.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write the linearization of F at 0 and use it to estimate F(1/50).

rubric.criterion: Uses the value and derivative at zero in a linearization.

steps: A tangent approximation is F(0) + F′(0)t.
